# Frame TV Art Manager: full documentation summary

> Plain-text digest of every guide on https://mikeo7.github.io/frame-tv-art-manager/ for AI search and answer engines. The short fact sheet is at https://mikeo7.github.io/frame-tv-art-manager/llms.txt.

Last substantive update: 2026-11-07
Source: https://github.com/MikeO7/frame-tv-art-manager
License: PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0. Free for personal and other noncommercial use. Source-available, not open source.
Affiliation: independent project; not affiliated with or endorsed by Samsung.

## Home: https://mikeo7.github.io/frame-tv-art-manager/

Q: What is Frame TV Art Manager?
A: Frame TV Art Manager is a free, self-hosted service for Samsung The Frame owners. It runs in Docker on a NAS or home server and keeps the TV's Art Mode in sync with a folder of JPEG and PNG pictures, preparing each one for the 3840×2160 screen and uploading it over your home network.

Q: Do I need a Samsung Art Store subscription?
A: No. Frame TV Art Manager uploads your own pictures and free art you choose, which don't need the Art Store. It doesn't unlock or touch Samsung's paid catalog. Your art also keeps changing on screen without one: the manager picks the next picture itself instead of relying on the TV's slideshow, which some owners report needs a subscription.

Q: Do I need SmartThings or a Samsung account?
A: No. It talks to the TV directly on your local network. Only optional online sources such as museums or NASA, and images an AI assistant asks it to fetch, contact the internet, and only when you turn them on.

Q: How does it handle portrait photos?
A: By default portraits are shown whole on a deep charcoal gallery mat, faintly tinted toward the picture's colors, instead of being cropped. You can also pair two portraits side by side, matched by color, or crop to fill the screen.

Q: Will it delete art I already put on my TV?
A: No. It only removes art it uploaded itself. Art you added with SmartThings, a USB stick, or anything else stays unless you deliberately set REMOVE_UNKNOWN_IMAGES=true.

Q: What happens when my Frame TV's storage is full?
A: It rotates the art it uploaded: each piece stays at least 14 days by default, then is swapped for art that hasn't been shown yet. Your own uploads and the files in your folder are never deleted.

Q: Will it upload the same photo twice?
A: No. Pictures are recognized by their contents, so a photo that is already on the TV is never sent again, even under a new name.

Q: Can I show Christmas or other holiday art only during the holidays?
A: Yes. Put the pictures in a themed collection with a yearly date window, such as December 1 to January 6. While the window is open the collection replaces your everyday art, or is shown alongside it if you choose. Afterwards the everyday art comes back on its own, and no files are deleted.

Q: Can an AI assistant like Claude or ChatGPT make art for my Frame TV?
A: Yes, through your own assistant. Turn on the optional MCP endpoint and connect an MCP client such as Claude Code or Claude Desktop. The assistant makes the images with its own tools; Frame TV Art Manager tells it the screen's size, prepares and previews the images, puts them in a themed collection, and schedules them. The app holds no AI account or API key.

Q: Does it keep my original photos?
A: Yes. Each picture's untouched original is kept in the artwork folder's hidden .frame-tv-art-manager/originals directory, and every prepared version is made from it, so you can change an image setting later without losing quality. Pictures prepared by earlier versions, which replaced originals outright, keep their current file as the original from then on.

Q: What can I run it on?
A: Anything that runs Docker and stays on: a Synology, Unraid, or TrueNAS NAS, a mini PC, a Raspberry Pi-class board, or a Mac. The image is built for amd64, arm64, and armv7.

Q: Which Frame TVs does it work with?
A: Samsung Frame TVs running Tizen 8.0 or newer. Older firmware may work, but Samsung's private Art Mode protocol changes between models and releases. Several TVs can be managed at once.

Q: Is Frame TV Art Manager free and open source?
A: It is free for personal and other noncommercial use under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0. The code is public, but commercial use isn't permitted, so it is source-available rather than open source. It is not affiliated with Samsung.

## Samsung Frame TV art without a subscription

URL: https://mikeo7.github.io/frame-tv-art-manager/guides/frame-tv-art-without-subscription.html

Short answer: you don't need Samsung's Art Store to enjoy The Frame. Your own photos in My Photos are free to display, and museums publish thousands of public-domain paintings you can use at no cost. Frame TV Art Manager, a free self-hosted service, keeps a folder of that art on the TV for you: it prepares each picture for the 4K screen, uploads it over your home network, changes the picture on screen every 15 minutes, and swaps art in and out when the TV is full.

### What costs money on The Frame, and what doesn't
The Samsung Art Store is a paid subscription: US$4.99 a month or US$49.99 a year
as reported in October 2026, with prices varying by country. It unlocks Samsung's licensed catalog of paintings and photography.
Your own pictures are a different matter. Photos you add to the My Photos collection, from the SmartThings
app, a USB stick, or a tool like Frame TV Art Manager, don't need a subscription to display. Samsung's own
Art Mode page describes showing all of My Photos as free for personal photo collections.
About the slideshow reports. Since about July 2025, some owners have reported on
Samsung's community forum that the "Display All" slideshow of My Photos asked them for an
Art Store subscription. Samsung's help pages still describe it as free, and the behavior seems to vary by model and
firmware. On a 2024 Frame we tested, the TV accepted the slideshow setting but never changed the picture. Choosing a
picture directly still works without a subscription, so Frame TV Art Manager changes the picture itself
instead of relying on the TV's slideshow. The options below work either way.

### Three ways to fill Art Mode for free
1. Your own photos
Family photos, travel shots, and your kids' drawings all work. The catch with doing it by hand is the routine: one
upload at a time from a phone, portraits that get cropped, and a TV that eventually runs out of room.
Automatic uploads turn that into "drop files in a folder".
2. Public-domain masterpieces
The Art Institute of Chicago, The Met, the Cleveland Museum of Art, SMK, the National Gallery of Art, the Rijksmuseum, and the Smithsonian publish
high-resolution images of public-domain works for anyone to use. Van Gogh, Monet, Hokusai, Vermeer, and Seurat are all
there. Frame TV Art Manager downloads from the first four with no API key, for example museum:search:winter to search them all at once.
The free 4K art guide lists where to look and how to
pull art in automatically.
3. Free photo and space imagery
Wikimedia Commons' Picture of the Day and Featured Pictures, NASA's image library and Astronomy Picture of the Day, Unsplash, Pexels, and Pixabay offer free images under their own
licenses. Frame TV Art Manager can download from all of them on a schedule; Wikimedia Commons needs no key, NASA works with its shared DEMO_KEY, and Unsplash, Pexels, and Pixabay need a free API key.

### How to keep the art changing without a subscription
A Frame looks best when the art changes now and then. Frame TV Art Manager handles the parts that are tedious by hand:
- New art arrives on its own. Pictures you add to the folder, and art from online sources, are uploaded on the next sync (every 30 minutes by default).
- A large collection takes turns. When the TV is full, each piece the manager uploaded stays for 14 days (ROTATION_INTERVAL_DAYS) and is then swapped for art that hasn't been shown yet.
- The picture changes on its own. Every 15 minutes by default, the manager puts a different piece it uploaded on screen; no Art Store subscription is needed. SLIDESHOW_INTERVAL sets the minutes, from 1 to 1440, and SLIDESHOW_TYPE the order: shuffle (the default) shows every picture once, in a new random order each round, before any repeats, and sequential goes in name order. It changes the picture only while the TV is in Art Mode and can confirm what's on screen, never while someone is watching TV.
- Nothing is uploaded twice. Pictures are recognized by their content, so re-adding the same file doesn't create duplicates on the TV.
- Holiday art on its own schedule. A themed collection shows Christmas or Halloween art only on the dates you choose, then your everyday art returns.
- Your AI assistant can help. With the optional MCP endpoint, an assistant such as Claude can make or find art and schedule it; see the AI art guide. The manager itself needs no AI subscription or key.
The manager changes the picture itself because choosing a picture directly works without a subscription, while the TV's own slideshow of My Photos may not. Set SLIDESHOW_ENABLED=false to leave the choice to the TV. If you subscribe to the Art Store and prefer the TV's own slideshow, set SLIDESHOW_MODE=tv; SLIDESHOW_INTERVAL must then be 3, 15, 60, 720, or 1440, and the manager never picks the picture. Either way, it never deletes art you put on the TV yourself.

### What you need
- A Samsung Frame TV running Tizen 8.0 or newer. Older firmware may work, but Samsung's private Art Mode protocol changes between models and releases.
- An always-on computer on the same network: a Synology, Unraid, or TrueNAS NAS, a mini PC, a Raspberry Pi-class board, or a Mac with Docker.
- About ten minutes for the Docker setup. The only required setting is the TV's IP address.
No Samsung account, SmartThings account, or cloud service is involved; the service talks to the TV directly on your network.

### What Frame TV Art Manager costs
Nothing for home use. Frame TV Art Manager is free for personal and other noncommercial use under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0; it is source-available, not open source. Commercial use, for example in a shop, office, or hotel, is not permitted.
It is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Samsung.

Q: Do I need a subscription to show my own photos on The Frame?
A: No. Photos in My Photos can be displayed without the Art Store subscription. Some owners have reported since July 2025 that the Display All slideshow of My Photos asked for a subscription on their TVs; Samsung's help pages still describe it as free.

Q: Can The Frame cycle through my own photos without a subscription?
A: Yes. Frame TV Art Manager changes the picture itself, every 15 minutes by default, choosing among the art it uploaded while the TV is in Art Mode. It doesn't rely on the TV's own slideshow, which some owners report needs an Art Store subscription.

Q: How much is the Samsung Art Store?
A: As reported in October 2026, US$4.99 per month or US$49.99 per year in the US. Prices vary by country, so check the Art Store on your TV.

Q: Where can I get free art for a Samsung Frame TV?
A: Museum open-access collections such as the Art Institute of Chicago, The Met, the Cleveland Museum of Art, SMK, the National Gallery of Art, and the Rijksmuseum publish public-domain works for free. Wikimedia Commons, NASA, Unsplash, Pexels, and Pixabay offer free images under their own licenses. Frame TV Art Manager downloads from the first four museums and Wikimedia Commons with no API key.

Q: Can Frame TV Art Manager unlock Art Store content?
A: No. It does not touch the Art Store or Samsung's licensed catalog. It only uploads your own pictures and art you choose from free sources.

Q: Is Frame TV Art Manager really free?
A: Yes, for personal and other noncommercial use under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0. There is no paid tier and no account to create.

## How to upload photos to a Samsung Frame TV automatically

URL: https://mikeo7.github.io/frame-tv-art-manager/guides/automatically-upload-art-samsung-frame-tv.html

Short answer: run Frame TV Art Manager on a NAS or home server, give it your Frame TV's IP address, and put JPEG or PNG files in its artwork folder. It uploads new pictures at startup and every 30 minutes, removes ones you delete from the folder, never uploads the same picture twice, and leaves art you added yourself alone. No SmartThings app or Samsung account is needed.

### Every way to get photos onto The Frame
Ways to upload your own photos to a Samsung Frame TV
- Method | Good for | Drawbacks
- SmartThings app | A few photos from your phone | One batch at a time, by hand, per TV; a Samsung account
- USB stick | A one-off batch without a phone | Walking to the TV for every change
- Frame TV Art Manager | A collection that changes, several TVs, large libraries | Needs an always-on computer running Docker
The first two are Samsung's built-in options. This guide covers the third: a folder that the TV follows on its own.

### What "automatic" means here
Frame TV Art Manager treats a folder as the list of art that should be on your Frame. At startup and every
30 minutes after (SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES), it compares the folder with what's stored on each TV, uploads anything
missing, and removes pieces it uploaded that you have since deleted from the folder. You never open an app.

### What you need
- A Samsung Frame TV running Tizen 8.0 or newer, on your home network.
- An always-on machine on the same network that runs Docker: a NAS, Unraid server, mini PC, Raspberry Pi-class board, or Mac.
- A fixed IP address for each TV, set with a DHCP reservation in your router.
- Pictures as JPEG (.jpg, .jpeg) or PNG (.png). iPhone HEIC photos need converting first; the Apple Photos guide shows how.
The Docker guide walks through installation. The only required setting is TV_IPS.

### How each sync works
- Download anything new from your online sources, if you set any up.
- Check the folder and prepare pictures that need it: turned upright, fitted to the 16:9 screen, converted to sRGB, and resized to 3840×2160.
- Read each TV to see what's stored on it.
- Upload what's missing and remove pieces you deleted from the folder.
- Apply TV settings such as brightness, power-off, or the TV's own slideshow, only if you configured them.
Between syncs, the manager also changes the picture on screen every 15 minutes by default, choosing only art it uploaded and only while the TV is in Art Mode. Set SLIDESHOW_ENABLED=false to leave that to the TV.
If you use themed collections, each sync also picks which pictures are wanted today, for example only the Christmas art from December 1 to January 6. Pictures that aren't wanted today are removed from the TV but stay in the folder.
The prepared version of each picture replaces it in the artwork folder, and the untouched original is kept in the folder's hidden .frame-tv-art-manager/originals directory. Prepared versions are always re-made from the original, so changing an image setting later never costs quality.

### Why you never get duplicates
A common complaint with upload scripts is the same photos piling up on the TV again and again. Frame TV Art
Manager identifies each picture by a hash of its contents and keeps a per-TV record of what it uploaded. A picture that is
already on the TV is never sent again, renaming a file doesn't make it new, and two identical files in the folder are stored once.

### Removing art
Delete a picture from the folder and the next sync removes the copy the manager uploaded. If the folder becomes
completely empty, the last piece stays on the TV so a mistake can't leave the screen blank. Art you added through
SmartThings or USB is never removed unless you deliberately set REMOVE_UNKNOWN_IMAGES=true.

### Several Frame TVs, one folder
List every TV in TV_IPS, separated by commas, for example TV_IPS=192.168.1.150,192.168.1.151.
Each TV gets the same collection and is tracked separately, so a TV that's off doesn't hold up the others.

### Adding art from your phone and the web
- Network share: copy files into the artwork folder from any computer.
- Upload page: turn on UPLOAD_ENABLED and open http://SERVER-IP:8080/upload in a browser. It also accepts iPhone Shortcuts and curl; see the Apple Photos guide.
- Online sources: public-domain works from the Art Institute of Chicago, The Met, the Cleveland Museum of Art, and SMK, and Wikimedia Commons' Picture of the Day and Featured Pictures, all with no API key; plus NASA, Unsplash, Pexels, Pixabay, and direct image links. See the free art guide.
- An AI assistant: with the optional MCP endpoint, Claude or another assistant can add images it makes or finds, preview them, and schedule them; see the AI art guide.

### What it won't do
- Delete art you added yourself, unless REMOVE_UNKNOWN_IMAGES=true.
- Change the picture while someone is watching TV, or put art it didn't upload on screen.
- Change anything on a TV whose state it can't confirm. That TV is skipped until the next sync.
- Treat a failed folder scan or a website that's down as "delete everything". A failing source keeps its last good results, and the rest of the sync goes ahead.
- Change anything at all in a dry run (DRY_RUN=true).

Q: Can I upload photos to a Samsung Frame TV without the SmartThings app?
A: Yes. Samsung's own alternative is a USB stick. Frame TV Art Manager is another: it uploads from a folder over your local network without SmartThings or a Samsung account.

Q: How often does Frame TV Art Manager upload new art?
A: At startup and then every 30 minutes by default. Change it with SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES.

Q: Will it upload the same photo twice?
A: No. Pictures are identified by their contents, so a photo already on the TV is never uploaded again, even if you rename or re-copy the file.

Q: Can it delete photos from the Frame TV for me?
A: Yes, but only the ones it uploaded. Delete the picture from the folder and the next sync removes it from the TV. Art you added another way stays.

Q: Does it work with more than one Frame TV?
A: Yes. List each TV's IP address in TV_IPS, separated by commas. Every TV is kept in sync with the same folder.

## Portrait photos on Samsung The Frame: a gallery mat, not a crop

URL: https://mikeo7.github.io/frame-tv-art-manager/guides/samsung-frame-tv-portrait-photos-mat.html

Short answer: The Frame's screen is a 16:9 landscape, so a portrait photo either gets cropped, which often cuts off heads, or needs a border. Frame TV Art Manager shows portraits, square art, panoramas, and small images whole on a deep charcoal gallery mat, faintly tinted from the art's own colors and calm in a dark room. You can also pair two portraits side by side or keep cropping.

### Why portraits look wrong on The Frame
A portrait photo is taller than it is wide; The Frame is 16:9 wide. Filling the screen means throwing away
most of the picture's height, usually the top and bottom, which is where heads and feet are. Samsung's mattes add a
border, but owners often find the default off-white matte too bright, especially at night.

### Before and after
A portrait painting
Cropped to fill
Cropped to fill the screen: the younger sister is reduced to the top of her hat.
Frame TV Art Manager default
Shown whole on the gallery mat, set slightly above center as framers do.
A nearly square painting
Cropped to fill
Cropped: almost 30% of the painting, including the village, is gone.
Frame TV Art Manager default
Matted: the whole painting, on a charcoal mat tinted toward its blues.
A landscape that already fits
Hokusai's Great Wave loses about 16% from the top and bottom, within the 25% limit, so it fills the screen. Cropping is still the right call when little is lost.
Artwork: Pierre-Auguste Renoir, Two Sisters (On the Terrace), 1881, Art Institute of Chicago, public domain (CC0).
Vincent van Gogh, The Starry Night, 1889, public domain. Katsushika Hokusai, The Great Wave off Kanagawa, c. 1831, public domain.
Every image on this page was rendered by Frame TV Art Manager at 3840×2160 and scaled down for the web.

### When it crops and when it mats
Every picture goes through the same decision:
- Landscape pictures fill the screen when cropping removes at most 25% of the image (IMAGE_MAX_CROP_PERCENT) and filling needs no more than 3× enlargement (IMAGE_MAX_UPSCALE). That covers 3:2 camera photos and 4:3 paintings.
- Everything else is shown whole: square art, very wide panoramas, and small images that would turn to mush if blown up.
- Portraits follow PORTRAIT_MODE: pad (default, shown whole), collage (paired side by side), or crop (fill the screen).
Set IMAGE_MAX_CROP_PERCENT=100 if you always want the screen filled.

### How the gallery mat looks
- Deep charcoal by default. It stays calm in a dark room at night instead of glowing like a white border.
- Tinted from the art. The mat is faintly shifted toward the picture's own colors, so it looks chosen rather than generic.
- A lighter bevel around the opening, and the opening sits slightly above center, the way picture framers cut mats.
- A soft warm greige (never bright white) is used only when the art's edge is too dark to stand out against charcoal. Force either tone with IMAGE_MAT_TONE=dark or light.
- Prefer a blurred backdrop? IMAGE_PAD_STYLE=blur fills the screen with a darkened, desaturated blur of the image instead.

### Two portraits side by side
With PORTRAIT_MODE=collage, portraits are paired on one screen. Pairs are matched by color,
lightness, and shape, so a warm sunset portrait isn't stuck next to a cold blue one. Both images appear whole, at equal
height, in a double-opening gallery mat. A portrait without a good partner waits for one instead of being forced into a bad pair.

### Samsung's own mattes
The Frame can also draw its own matte around a picture. MATTE_STYLE sets one for every upload, as
style_color: styles include modernthin, modern, modernwide, flexible,
shadowbox, panoramic, triptych, mix, and squares; colors include
black, neutral, antique, warm, polar, sand, sage,
navy, and more. The default is none, full screen.
For one picture, add a mattes.json file to the artwork folder:
{
"_default": "none",
"wedding-portrait.jpg": "shadowbox_polar"
}
An override keeps working after the manager renames the file. An invalid mattes.json stops the sync before any TV is touched, so a typo can't go unnoticed.
The gallery mat is part of the picture itself, so with the default MATTE_STYLE=none you won't get a border inside a border.
PORTRAIT_MATTE sets the matte the TV uses when it shows art in portrait orientation; it defaults to the same value as MATTE_STYLE.
Before each upload the manager checks the matte against the list the TV reports, and a matte the TV doesn't offer is replaced with none and logged as a warning.

### Settings at a glance
Portrait and mat settings
- Setting | Default | What it does
- PORTRAIT_MODE | pad | pad, collage, or crop
- IMAGE_PAD_STYLE | mat | mat (gallery mat) or blur
- IMAGE_MAT_TONE | auto | auto, dark, or light
- IMAGE_MAX_CROP_PERCENT | 25 | Most of a landscape picture that may be cropped away
- IMAGE_MAX_UPSCALE | 3 | Largest enlargement before a picture is matted instead
- SMART_CROP_ENABLED | false | Crop toward the interesting part instead of the center
- MATTE_STYLE | none | Samsung's own matte for every upload
- PORTRAIT_MATTE | same as MATTE_STYLE | Samsung's matte when the TV shows art in portrait orientation

Q: How do I show portrait photos on a Samsung Frame TV without cropping?
A: Use a border instead of a crop. Frame TV Art Manager does this by default: portraits are shown whole on a charcoal gallery mat tinted toward the photo's colors. Samsung's own mattes are another option.

Q: Why does my Frame TV crop my photos?
A: The Frame's screen is 16:9. Any picture with a different shape has to be either cropped or bordered to fill it, and portraits lose the most.

Q: Can I put two portrait photos side by side on The Frame?
A: Yes. With PORTRAIT_MODE=collage, Frame TV Art Manager pairs portraits matched by color, lightness, and shape and shows both whole in a double-opening mat.

Q: How do I get rid of the white matte on my Frame TV?
A: Choose a different matte or none in Art Mode on the TV. With Frame TV Art Manager, MATTE_STYLE=none (the default) uploads without a Samsung matte, and the gallery mat is charcoal rather than white.

Q: Will a gallery mat make my photo smaller?
A: Yes, a portrait shown whole is narrower than the screen. That's the trade-off for keeping heads and edges intact. Set PORTRAIT_MODE=crop if you prefer to fill the screen.

## Free public-domain 4K art for Samsung The Frame

URL: https://mikeo7.github.io/frame-tv-art-manager/guides/free-public-domain-art-samsung-frame-tv.html

Short answer: major museums publish high-resolution images of public-domain paintings for anyone to use. Frame TV Art Manager downloads them with no API key from the Art Institute of Chicago, The Met, the Cleveland Museum of Art, and SMK (the National Gallery of Denmark), and from Wikimedia Commons' Picture of the Day and Featured Pictures. One line, museum:search:winter, searches all four museums at once and keeps only public-domain works. NASA, Unsplash, Pexels, and Pixabay work too, and every image is prepared for the TV's 3840×2160 screen.

### Where to find free art for The Frame
Five sources are built in and need no account or API key. The others work through a direct image link or a free key.
Free sources of high-resolution art and photography
- Source | What's there | Terms | Automatic download
- Art Institute of Chicago | Impressionism, American art, Japanese prints | Public-domain works released under CC0 | Yes, no key (art_institute_of_chicago)
- The Met Open Access | Paintings, prints, and objects from every era | Public-domain works released under CC0 | Yes, no key (met)
- Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access | Paintings, prints, and objects from many cultures | CC0 works only | Yes, no key (cleveland)
- SMK, National Gallery of Denmark | Danish and European art, including Hammershøi | Public-domain works | Yes, no key (smk)
- Wikimedia Commons | Picture of the Day and Featured Pictures: photography, nature, paintings | Often CC BY or CC BY-SA, which require credit | Yes, no key (commons)
- National Gallery of Art | European and American painting | Open-access public-domain images | Via direct links
- Rijksmuseum | Dutch Golden Age: Vermeer, Rembrandt | Public-domain images free to download | Via direct links; not a built-in source
- Smithsonian Open Access | Art, nature, and history | CC0 items marked as such | Via direct links
- NASA | Space telescopes, Earth from orbit, Astronomy Picture of the Day | Generally free to use; see NASA's media guidelines | Yes, free key or DEMO_KEY
- Unsplash, Pexels, Pixabay | Modern photography | Each site's own free license | Yes, free API key
"Public domain" means the copyright has expired; museums that release those images under CC0 put no conditions on them.
Each site's terms are its own and can change, so check them before relying on an image. Note that NASA's APOD sometimes features
images credited to other photographers, under their own terms.

### Download art to The Frame automatically
Frame TV Art Manager can fetch art for you. Set ARTWORK_SOURCES_FILE=/data/sources.yaml; if the file
doesn't exist, a commented starter file is created. A sources file looks like this:
providers:
museum:
- search:winter landscape # up to 20 works mixed across four museums
met:
- search:sunflowers
- object:436524 # one work by its ID
cleveland:
- search:snow?type=Painting # a search narrowed with a filter
smk:
- search:hammershøi
art_institute_of_chicago:
- photo:20684
commons:
- potd # Wikimedia Commons Picture of the Day
- featured # the 10 newest Featured Pictures
nasa:
- apod # NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day
direct:
- https://example.com/painting.jpg
Downloads land in your artwork folder like any other picture, are prepared for the screen, and are uploaded on the next
sync. If a source fails, nothing previously downloaded is removed and the rest of the sync goes ahead. Removing a line from the file doesn't delete what it
already downloaded; delete those files yourself.
- How much each line brings in: a museum search takes its first 10 results; museum:search takes up to 20, mixed across the museums.
- Sized for 4K: images are requested just large enough to cover 3840×2160, with a smaller version as a fallback when the large one is over MAX_DOWNLOAD_SIZE_MB (20 MB by default) or 40 megapixels. Cleveland, SMK, and Commons images under 1920 pixels on the long edge are skipped.
- Gentle on the museums: results are cached for 24 hours, rate limits are respected, and a provider that fails keeps its last good results.
A sources file adds art to your everyday collection, which shows all year. To show winter or holiday art only on certain dates, put it in a themed collection.

### Search four museums by theme
museum:search:<theme> searches the Art Institute of Chicago, The Met, the Cleveland Museum of Art, and SMK at once and mixes their results.
When two museums hold copies of the same work by the same artist, common for prints, only one is kept. If one museum is down, the others' works are still used.
Public domain only. Searches of the Art Institute of Chicago, The Met, and SMK return only public-domain works, and Cleveland searches return only CC0 works.
The public-domain and has-image filters are always applied, and unknown filters are rejected, so a typo can't widen a search.
Each museum can also be searched on its own, and The Met and Cleveland accept filters after a ?, written as name=value pairs joined by &:
- The Met: departmentId, isHighlight, isOnView, artistOrCulture, title, tags, medium, geoLocation, dateBegin, dateEnd. For example, met:search:?isHighlight=true&departmentId=11; the query before the ? may be empty when a filter is given.
- Cleveland: type (such as Painting or Print), department, highlight, artists, title, created_after, created_before, currently_on_view.
- SMK takes no filters.
To add one work, use its ID from the museum's page: metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/436524 is met:object:436524,
clevelandart.org/art/1997.111 is cleveland:object:1997.111, open.smk.dk/artwork/image/KMS1 is smk:object:KMS1,
and artic.edu/artworks/27992/… is art_institute_of_chicago:photo:27992.

### Wikimedia Commons pictures and credit
Wikimedia Commons is a free media library whose community picks Featured Pictures and a Picture of the Day. commons:potd adds one picture a day
(it changes at midnight UTC), commons:featured takes the 10 newest Featured Pictures, and commons:search:northern lights takes 10 Featured Pictures matching a query.
Commons files are often CC BY or CC BY-SA, which require crediting the author and license. Frame TV Art Manager records the title, artist, provider,
source page, and license of every downloaded image under attributions in /status, for museum works too, and skips Commons files without license information.

### What makes art look good on The Frame
- Landscape works fill the screen best. Paintings close to 16:9, 3:2, or 4:3 are cropped only slightly; square and tall works are shown whole on a gallery mat.
- Resolution matters. Aim for images at least 3840 pixels wide. Images that would need more than 3× enlargement are matted rather than blown up into blur.
- Matte finish suits paintings. Oil paintings, watercolors, and prints look more like real art on The Frame's matte screen than glossy photographs do.
- Change with the seasons. Searches such as museum:search:snow or museum:search:autumn give the collection a seasonal feel, and a themed collection shows holiday art only on the dates you choose.
See the art size guide for exactly what happens to each shape.

### A few public-domain favorites
- Georges Seurat, A Sunday on La Grande Jatte, 1884 to 1886, Art Institute of Chicago.
- Katsushika Hokusai, The Great Wave off Kanagawa, about 1831, in many museum collections.
- Claude Monet's Water Lilies and Stacks of Wheat series.
- Vincent van Gogh, The Bedroom, 1889, Art Institute of Chicago.
- Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Harvesters, 1565, The Met.
- Vilhelm Hammershøi's quiet interiors, SMK.

### Let your AI assistant choose the paintings
With the optional MCP endpoint turned on, an AI assistant such as Claude can search the same four museums for you
(search_public_domain_art), add the works you like to a themed collection with their title, artist, license, and museum link,
preview how each will be fitted to the screen, and schedule the collection. The manager holds no AI keys; see
AI art for The Frame with MCP.

Q: Where can I get free art for my Samsung Frame TV?
A: Museum open-access programs at The Met, the Art Institute of Chicago, the Cleveland Museum of Art, SMK, the National Gallery of Art, the Rijksmuseum, and the Smithsonian publish public-domain artwork for free, and Wikimedia Commons curates Featured Pictures. NASA, Unsplash, Pexels, and Pixabay offer free images under their own terms.

Q: Is public-domain art free to display on my TV?
A: Yes. Public-domain works are no longer under copyright, and museums that release images under CC0 put no conditions on using them. Wikimedia Commons files are often CC BY or CC BY-SA, which require crediting the author, and photo sites such as Unsplash use their own licenses, so check each one.

Q: Can Frame TV Art Manager download art automatically?
A: Yes. List sources in a sources file and it downloads from the Art Institute of Chicago, The Met, the Cleveland Museum of Art, SMK, Wikimedia Commons, NASA, Unsplash, Pexels, Pixabay, and direct image links on each sync, then prepares and uploads the art.

Q: Do I need an API key for museum art?
A: No. The Art Institute of Chicago, The Met, the Cleveland Museum of Art, SMK, and Wikimedia Commons need no key. Unsplash, Pexels, and Pixabay need a free key, and NASA works with its shared DEMO_KEY or a free key of your own.

Q: Do the museum searches only return public-domain works?
A: Yes. Searches of the Art Institute of Chicago, The Met, and SMK return only public-domain works, and Cleveland searches return only CC0 works. The public-domain and has-image filters are always applied.

Q: What resolution should free art be for The Frame?
A: At least 3840 pixels wide for the 4K models. Smaller images are shown whole on a gallery mat instead of being enlarged into blur.

## Seasonal and holiday art collections on the Samsung Frame TV

URL: https://mikeo7.github.io/frame-tv-art-manager/guides/seasonal-art-collections-samsung-frame-tv.html

Short answer: Frame TV Art Manager can show Christmas, Halloween, or spring art on The Frame only on the dates you choose. Put the pictures in a themed collection with a yearly window, such as December 1 to January 6. While the window is open, the collection replaces your everyday art (exclusive, the default) or is shown alongside it. When the window closes, the holiday pictures come off the TV and your everyday art returns by itself. No files are deleted, and art you added to the TV yourself is never touched.

### How a themed collection works
A themed collection is a named group of pictures from your artwork folder, such as "Christmas", that is shown only when its schedule says so.
Without any collections nothing changes: every picture in the folder is part of the normal rotation. Each collection has one of three schedules:
Themed collection schedules
- Schedule | When it is active
- always | Always.
- off | Never. New collections start here, so nothing changes on the TV until you schedule one.
- window | Every year from a start date to an end date, written as MM-DD and including both days. A window can run across New Year, such as 12-01 to 01-06. 02-29 is allowed and simply doesn't occur in other years.
Dates follow LOCATION_TIMEZONE, the same clock as AUTO_OFF_TIME (UTC by default), so a window opens at midnight where the TV is.
The change reaches the TV on the first sync after midnight, within 30 minutes by default.

### Replace your everyday art, or add to it
Pictures that belong to no collection are your everyday art. Each sync picks what to show like this:
- Exclusive (the default): while an exclusive collection is active and holds at least one picture, only pictures from active collections are shown. Your Christmas art replaces the everyday art.
- Not exclusive: an active collection is shown together with the everyday art. Good for a light seasonal touch, such as spring flowers mixed into your usual photos.
- Out of season: a picture that belongs only to inactive collections is hidden, and its copy is removed from the TV like any picture that left the folder. A picture in several collections is shown while any of them is active.
Hiding a picture never deletes its file. The manager's other rules still apply: it never removes art you put on the TV yourself, and its picture changes only choose among the pieces it keeps on the TV, so hidden pictures don't come up.

### A year of art: Christmas, Halloween, and spring
Three collections cover most of a year: Christmas, exclusive, from 12-01 to 01-06; Halloween, exclusive, from 10-01 to 10-31; and Spring, not exclusive, from 03-20 to 06-20. Here is what the TV shows on a few dates:
What the Frame shows with three seasonal collections
- Date | Active | On the TV
- April 10 | Spring | Everyday art plus the spring pictures
- October 15 | Halloween | Halloween pictures only
- November 7 | None | Everyday art only; all seasonal pictures hidden
- December 24 | Christmas | Christmas pictures only
- January 7 | None | Everyday art only
An exclusive collection with no pictures in the folder doesn't replace anything, so an empty Halloween collection leaves your everyday art up.

### Create and schedule a collection
With an AI assistant
The easiest way is an AI assistant connected over MCP. Ask for "a Christmas collection shown December 1 to January 6" and it adds the
pictures, then sets the schedule with update_collection and starts a sync. It can make new images or find public-domain paintings.
The AI art guide shows the setup and a full example.
By hand
Collections live in .frame-tv-art-manager/collections.json inside the artwork folder, for example data/artwork/.frame-tv-art-manager/collections.json.
The file must be readable only by the service user (chmod 600). Each member names a picture by its key; the assistant's
list_artwork tool reports every picture's key.
{
"version": 1,
"collections": [
{
"slug": "christmas",
"name": "Christmas",
"exclusive": true,
"activation": { "mode": "window", "start": "12-01", "end": "01-06" },
"members": [
{ "key": "snowy-canal.jpg", "added_at": "2026-11-07T00:00:00Z" }
]
},
{
"slug": "halloween",
"name": "Halloween",
"exclusive": true,
"activation": { "mode": "window", "start": "10-01", "end": "10-31" },
"members": []
},
{
"slug": "spring",
"name": "Spring",
"exclusive": false,
"activation": { "mode": "window", "start": "03-20", "end": "06-20" },
"members": []
}
]
}
Membership follows each picture's stable identity, so renaming a picture, or re-preparing it after a settings change, keeps it in its collection.
One limitation: two portraits joined into a side-by-side collage become a new picture that belongs to no collection.

### Fill a collection with public-domain paintings
Museums hold centuries of winter scenes, harvests, and spring gardens, free to use. Two ways to bring them in:
- Into a collection, through your assistant. Its search_public_domain_art tool searches the Art Institute of Chicago, The Met, the Cleveland Museum of Art, and SMK at once. Pick the works you want and add_artwork stores each one in the collection with its title, artist, license, and museum link.
- Into your everyday art, through a sources file. A line such as museum:search:christmas downloads up to 20 public-domain works mixed across the same four museums. Downloads join the everyday art, which shows all year, so add them to a collection afterwards if they should be seasonal.
The free art guide covers every museum source, search filters, and credits.

### Collections on a full TV
Themed collections decide which pictures are wanted today. Rotation and MAX_ARTWORK_IMAGES then work on those pictures only.
- When an exclusive collection opens, the everyday pieces the manager uploaded are no longer wanted, so they are removed from the TV and the holiday pictures are uploaded in their place. When it closes, the reverse happens and the everyday art is uploaded again. Expect a busy sync at both ends of the window.
- If the collection is bigger than the TV holds, it rotates within itself: each piece stays at least ROTATION_INTERVAL_DAYS (14 by default). A five-week Christmas window shows about three rounds at 14 days; set a shorter interval, such as 3, if you want more of the set to appear.
- A non-exclusive collection on a full TV waits its turn: its pictures join the queue, and pieces never shown go first, but a slot only opens when a piece on the TV has stayed its full interval.
- Art you uploaded to the TV yourself is never rotated or removed, and it takes up space the collections can't use.

### If the collections file has a mistake
If collections.json can't be read, for example after a typo, the manager never shows or removes art based on a guess. It keeps the last collections it read
successfully since it started and reports the sync as failed in /status and /health until you fix the file. If it has never read the file,
it skips the TV work for that sync and reports the error. Tools that change collections refuse to overwrite a file they can't read, and with
DRY_RUN=true collections are evaluated but never saved.

Q: Can I show Christmas art on my Frame TV only in December?
A: Yes. Put the pictures in a themed collection with a yearly window, such as 12-01 to 12-31 or 12-01 to 01-06. Frame TV Art Manager shows them only while the window is open, in your LOCATION_TIMEZONE.

Q: What happens to my everyday art during the holidays?
A: With an exclusive collection, the default, the everyday pieces the manager uploaded come off the TV while the holiday collection is active and go back up when it ends. With a non-exclusive collection, both are shown.

Q: Are holiday pictures deleted after the season?
A: No. Their copies are removed from the TV, but the files stay in your artwork folder and come back the next year when the window opens again.

Q: Can a collection run over New Year?
A: Yes. A window whose end date is earlier than its start date, such as 12-01 to 01-06, wraps the new year. Both the start and end days are included.

Q: Do I need an AI assistant to use themed collections?
A: No. You can edit .frame-tv-art-manager/collections.json in the artwork folder by hand. An assistant connected over MCP just makes it easier to add pictures and set dates.

## Make AI art for your Samsung Frame TV with Claude or ChatGPT (MCP)

URL: https://mikeo7.github.io/frame-tv-art-manager/guides/ai-art-samsung-frame-tv-mcp.html

Short answer: Frame TV Art Manager has a built-in MCP endpoint, off by default, that lets your own AI assistant build art collections for your Samsung Frame TV. The assistant makes the images with its own tools; the manager holds no AI keys and calls no AI service. It tells the assistant the screen's exact size and format, stores and checks each image, previews how it will be fitted, puts it in a themed collection, schedules it, and syncs it to the TV. Turn it on with MCP_ENABLED=true and an MCP_TOKEN of at least 24 characters, then connect Claude Code, Claude Desktop, or another MCP client.

### What MCP is
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that lets an AI assistant use tools provided by
other programs. A program that speaks MCP, called a server, lists its tools with their names, inputs, and purpose, and the assistant
decides when to call them during a conversation. Frame TV Art Manager is an MCP server: when you ask your assistant for a Christmas
collection, it calls the manager's tools to read the TV's display spec, add the images, and set the dates.

### Why the manager needs no AI keys
The images come from your assistant, under your own account with it. Frame TV Art Manager never calls an AI service and stores no AI credentials. Its job is everything that happens after an image exists:
- Telling the assistant what the TV needs: 3840×2160 by default, 16:9, sRGB, JPEG or PNG, the size limit, and how other shapes are cropped or matted.
- Storing each image after checking it is a real JPEG or PNG, and recognizing duplicates by their contents.
- Showing a preview of each picture exactly as it will be prepared for the TV.
- Putting the pictures in a themed collection, scheduling it, and starting a sync.
If your assistant can't make images, it can still search public-domain museum collections, or add images from https links you give it.

### Set it up in four steps
Make a token
Run openssl rand -hex 24 and keep the result. The token must be at least 24 characters with no spaces.
Turn on the endpoint
Add MCP_ENABLED and MCP_TOKEN to the container's environment, as below, and run docker compose up -d.
Connect your assistant
Add the server to Claude Code or Claude Desktop with the commands below, or to any MCP client that supports streamable HTTP.
Check the connection
Ask "What does my Frame TV need from an image?" The assistant should call get_display_spec and answer with the screen's size.
compose.yaml (add to the service's environment)
environment:
MCP_ENABLED: "true"
MCP_TOKEN: "paste-the-output-of: openssl rand -hex 24"
The endpoint is http://<server-address>:8080/mcp (port HEALTH_PORT, which must stay on), and every request must send
Authorization: Bearer <MCP_TOKEN>. While MCP_ENABLED is off, the address returns 404.
Claude Code
claude mcp add --transport http frame-tv http://<server-address>:8080/mcp \
--header "Authorization: Bearer <MCP_TOKEN>"
Claude Desktop
Claude Desktop connects through the mcp-remote bridge, which needs Node.js.
Add this to claude_desktop_config.json and restart Claude Desktop:
{
"mcpServers": {
"frame-tv": {
"command": "npx",
"args": ["mcp-remote", "http://<server-address>:8080/mcp", "--allow-http",
"--header", "Authorization:${FRAME_TV_AUTH}"],
"env": { "FRAME_TV_AUTH": "Bearer <MCP_TOKEN>" }
}
}
}
Use https:// and drop --allow-http when the manager is behind a TLS proxy.
ChatGPT and other MCP clients
Other clients use the streamable HTTP transport with the URL and header above. Whether an assistant can connect depends on two things:
its MCP support must let you send the Authorization header, and it must be able to reach your server. Claude Code and Claude Desktop
run on your computer, so they reach a server on your home network. An assistant that connects from its own cloud servers, rather than from
your computer, can't reach a home-network address; it would need the endpoint exposed behind a TLS reverse proxy (see Keep it safe).
Check your assistant's current documentation before exposing anything.

### The tools your assistant gets
MCP tools provided by Frame TV Art Manager
- Tool | What it does
- get_display_spec | The target size (3840×2160 by default), aspect ratio, formats, size limit, and how pictures that don't fit are cropped or matted, with prompt tips
- search_public_domain_art | Searches the Art Institute of Chicago, The Met, the Cleveland Museum of Art, and SMK for public-domain works
- add_artwork | Stores one JPEG or PNG (an https link or base64 data) in a collection, creating the collection if needed, and records its title, artist, license, and link
- preview_artwork | Shows a 960×540 preview of a picture exactly as it will be prepared for the TV; nothing is saved
- list_artwork | Lists stored pictures with their collections, whether today's rules show them, and which TVs hold them
- list_collections, create_collection, update_collection, delete_collection | Manage collections and their schedules
- remove_from_collection | Takes a picture out of a collection
- sync_now | Starts a sync now instead of waiting for the next one
- get_status | The last sync's result and each TV's state

### Example: a Christmas collection
This is how a typical request plays out, shortened. Your assistant's wording will differ; the tool calls are the same.
You: Make me 12 Christmas paintings in the style of Dutch winter landscapes and show them Dec 1 to Jan 6.
Assistant calls get_display_spec, learns the screen is 3840×2160 and 16:9, and generates 12 landscape images with its own image tool, in one painterly style, with no text or frames.
Assistant calls add_artwork once per image with the collection Christmas, a title, and the prompt as the description. The first call creates the collection, which starts off and exclusive.
Assistant calls preview_artwork to check how the pictures will be fitted, then update_collection with the schedule window, 12-01 to 01-06, and finally sync_now and get_status.
Assistant: The Christmas collection is scheduled from December 1 to January 6. Until then it stays hidden. On December 1 it replaces your everyday art, and on January 7 your everyday art comes back.
You: Add a few real winter paintings too.
Assistant calls search_public_domain_art for "winter", lists candidates with their title, artist, museum, and license, and adds the ones you pick with add_artwork, using each result's image link, license, and museum page.
The window opens at midnight in LOCATION_TIMEZONE (UTC by default), so set it to your own time zone. The seasonal collections guide explains schedules, exclusive and everyday art, and what happens on a full TV.

### Prompt tips for a matte art screen
The Frame's anti-reflection matte panel makes paintings look like paintings, but it is still a lit screen in your living room. get_display_spec hands your assistant these tips, and they work just as well in your own prompts:
- 16:9 landscape, highest resolution. Ask for a landscape composition at the highest resolution your image model supports, ideally exactly 3840×2160. Anything smaller than about 2560×1440 is visibly enlarged on a 4K screen. Keep the main subject away from the edges.
- Painterly and textured. Oil, gouache, watercolor, etching, and woodcut styles look most like real art on the matte screen; glossy photoreal renders look like a TV.
- Muted palettes, soft light. Avoid large pure-white or neon areas: they glow in a dark room at night.
- No text, frames, or watermarks. Leave out text, signatures, watermarks, borders, frames, and mats; the TV and the manager add their own.
- One style per set. Keep the style and palette the same across a collection so it feels curated.
A snowy Dutch canal at dusk with skaters and a windmill, painted in oil
with visible brushwork, muted blues and warm lamplight, 16:9 landscape,
no text, no signature, no frame.
Images that aren't exactly 16:9 are still handled: with the default settings, a landscape image fills the screen when that crops away at most 25%
and needs no more than 3× enlargement; otherwise it is shown whole on a gallery mat. preview_artwork shows exactly which. See the
art size guide for the details.

### What the assistant can't do
- Delete image files. Removing a picture from a collection, or deleting a collection, leaves the files in the folder.
- Put a picture on screen right now. There is no "show this picture now" tool; the TV changes only through the normal sync and the scheduled picture changes, with all of their safety checks.
- Fetch from your home network. Links must be https and point to the public internet; private addresses are refused, even after redirects.
- Get around the upload rules. Images must be JPEG or PNG, no larger than MAX_DOWNLOAD_SIZE_MB (20 MB by default), and are checked and deduplicated before they are kept.
- Change anything during a dry run. With DRY_RUN=true the read-only tools still work, and tools that would change anything are refused.
Most assistants hand over generated images as links, so image_url is usually the practical choice; base64 data works for smaller images.

### Keep it safe
- Off by default. Nothing listens at /mcp until you set MCP_ENABLED=true and a token.
- Treat the token like a password. Anyone with it can add art, change collections and their schedules, and start a sync, though not delete image files. Use a long random token, such as the output of openssl rand -hex 24.
- Keep it on your home network. If you expose the endpoint beyond it, put it behind a reverse proxy with TLS; the token is sent with every request. Never forward port 8080 from your router.
- Guessing is slowed down. Wrong tokens count toward the same per-address limit as upload passwords, and browser requests from other websites are refused.

Q: Do I need an OpenAI or Anthropic API key to make AI art for my Frame TV?
A: Not for Frame TV Art Manager. It holds no AI keys and calls no AI service. Your assistant makes the images under your own account with it, and the manager sizes, previews, schedules, and syncs them.

Q: Which AI assistants work with Frame TV Art Manager?
A: Claude Code, Claude Desktop through the mcp-remote bridge, and other MCP clients that support streamable HTTP with an Authorization header and can reach your server. An assistant that connects from its own cloud servers needs the endpoint exposed behind a TLS reverse proxy.

Q: Can the AI assistant delete my photos or change what's on screen?
A: No. No tool deletes image files, and there is no tool to show a picture right away. The TV changes only through the normal sync and the scheduled picture changes, with their safety checks.

Q: What size should AI-generated art be for The Frame?
A: A 16:9 landscape, ideally exactly 3840×2160 pixels, as JPEG or PNG. Anything smaller than about 2560×1440 is visibly enlarged on the 4K screen.

Q: Can my assistant use real paintings instead of AI images?
A: Yes. The search_public_domain_art tool searches the Art Institute of Chicago, The Met, the Cleveland Museum of Art, and SMK for public-domain works, and add_artwork records each one's title, artist, license, and museum link.

## Samsung Frame TV art size: 3840×2160 explained

URL: https://mikeo7.github.io/frame-tv-art-manager/guides/samsung-frame-tv-art-size.html

Short answer: make art for The Frame at 3840×2160 pixels, a 16:9 landscape, in the sRGB color space, saved as a high-quality JPEG. That matches the 4K panel exactly, so the TV doesn't have to crop or scale. The 32-inch Frame has a 1920×1080 panel. Frame TV Art Manager prepares every picture to this size automatically: it rotates it upright, converts its colors to sRGB, and crops it or sets it on a gallery mat to fit.

### Quick reference
Recommended image specification for Samsung The Frame
- Pixel size | 3840×2160 (4K models); 1920×1080 for the 32-inch model
- Aspect ratio | 16:9 landscape
- Color space | sRGB
- File format | JPEG, high quality; PNG also works
- Not accepted | HEIC (iPhone default), RAW, TIFF, WebP: convert to JPEG first
Check your model's specifications if you're unsure of its panel resolution. To prepare everything at 1080p, set
IMAGE_MAX_WIDTH=1920 and IMAGE_MAX_HEIGHT=1080.

### What happens to each shape
Frame TV Art Manager fills the screen only when cropping removes at most 25% of the picture
(IMAGE_MAX_CROP_PERCENT). Anything else is shown whole on a gallery mat.
How common aspect ratios fit a 16:9 Frame with default settings
- Shape | Typical source | Cropped away to fill | Result
- 16:9 | TV and phone landscape video frames | 0% | Fills the screen
- 2:1 | Wide panoramas | 11% | Fills the screen
- 3:2 | Most cameras | 16% | Fills the screen
- 21:9 | Ultra-wide crops | 24% | Fills the screen
- 4:3 | Phones, many paintings | 25% | Fills the screen
- 5:4 | Large-format photos, many paintings | 30% | Gallery mat
- 1:1 | Square posts, album art | 44% | Gallery mat
- 3:1 or wider | Long panoramas | 41% or more | Gallery mat
- Portrait | Phone portraits, portrait paintings | More than 50% | Follows PORTRAIT_MODE: gallery mat by default
See the portrait and mat guide for before-and-after examples.

### Small images and blur
Enlarging a small image can't add detail; it just makes it soft. Frame TV Art Manager fills the screen only
when that needs at most 3× enlargement (IMAGE_MAX_UPSCALE). A 1200×800 photo, for example, would need 3.2× and is
shown whole on a mat instead. Sharpening is also skipped on images enlarged more than 1.5×, because there's no detail to
recover and sharpening would only exaggerate the blur.

### Color: why sRGB
The Frame expects standard sRGB color. Pictures from cameras and editing apps often carry a different color
profile, such as Display P3 or Adobe RGB; shown without conversion, they look dull or oversaturated. Frame TV Art Manager
converts any embedded ICC color profile to sRGB, and tone-maps HDR PNGs to standard range so bright skies don't clip.

### How Frame TV Art Manager prepares each picture
- Rotates it upright using its EXIF orientation, so phone photos aren't sideways.
- Decides between a crop and a gallery mat using the rules above.
- Converts its color to sRGB and tone-maps HDR PNGs.
- Resizes it in linear light, which keeps fine bright detail such as stars or lace from darkening, to exactly 3840×2160.
- Applies halo-free, contrast-adaptive sharpening (skipped on images enlarged more than 1.5×).
- Saves JPEG at quality 95 with full 4:4:4 color, so red and blue edges stay crisp (IMAGE_JPEG_SUBSAMPLING=420 makes smaller files); PNGs stay PNG, including transparency.
A 24-megapixel camera photo takes about a second. The prepared file replaces the picture in the artwork folder, and the untouched original is kept in its hidden .frame-tv-art-manager/originals directory, so changing a setting later re-prepares the art from the original without losing quality. Originals take about as much disk space as the pictures you add.

### File size and limits
A 3840×2160 JPEG at quality 95 is usually a few megabytes. Downloads and web uploads are limited to 20 MB by
default (MAX_DOWNLOAD_SIZE_MB, 1–100). Files you copy into the artwork folder may be up to 200 MB
(MAX_LOCAL_FILE_SIZE_MB, 1–512); larger ones are skipped with a warning. Each image is processed within a 512 MB memory budget,
which is enough for an 8-bit 8K original, and images above 40 megapixels are left out with a warning in the log.
Making art with an AI image tool? Ask for a 16:9 landscape at the highest resolution it offers, ideally exactly 3840×2160; anything smaller than about
2560×1440 is visibly enlarged on the 4K screen. The AI art guide shows how an assistant connected over MCP reads this spec itself.

Q: What size should pictures be for a Samsung Frame TV?
A: 3840×2160 pixels for the 4K models, a 16:9 landscape. The 32-inch Frame has a 1920×1080 panel.

Q: What aspect ratio is The Frame?
A: 16:9. Pictures with other shapes are cropped or shown with a border.

Q: Should Frame TV art be JPEG or PNG?
A: High-quality JPEG in sRGB is the safest choice. PNG also works. iPhone HEIC photos must be converted to JPEG first.

Q: Why does my art look blurry on The Frame?
A: Usually because a small image was enlarged to fill the 4K screen. Use images at least 3840 pixels wide, or let Frame TV Art Manager show small images whole on a mat instead of blowing them up.

Q: Do I need to resize photos myself?
A: Not with Frame TV Art Manager. It rotates, color-converts, and resizes every picture to 3840×2160 automatically.

## Install Frame TV Art Manager with Docker

URL: https://mikeo7.github.io/frame-tv-art-manager/guides/samsung-frame-tv-docker.html

Short answer: run the ghcr.io/mikeo7/frame-tv-art-manager:latest image with your Samsung Frame TV's IP address in TV_IPS and a ./data:/data volume. Approve the connection once on the TV, then copy JPEG or PNG files into data/artwork. The image runs on amd64, arm64, and armv7, so it fits a NAS, a mini PC, a Raspberry Pi-class board, or a Mac.

### Before you start
- A Samsung Frame TV running Tizen 8.0 or newer, on the same network as the server.
- Docker with Compose on a machine that stays on.
- Access to your router, to give the TV a fixed address.

### Install in six steps
Give the TV a fixed IP address
In your router, create a DHCP reservation so the Frame always gets the same address. The TV shows its current address under its network settings.
Create the compose file
Make a folder for the service and save the compose.yaml below in it, with your TV's address.
Start the container
Run docker compose up -d, then docker compose logs -f frame-tv-art-manager to watch it connect.
Approve it on the TV
With the TV on, an Allow/Deny prompt named "Frame Art Manager" appears. Choose Allow with the remote. You only do this once.
Add pictures
Copy .jpg, .jpeg, or .png files into data/artwork. Each file is replaced by its prepared version, and the untouched original is kept in the hidden data/artwork/.frame-tv-art-manager/originals folder.
Check that it worked
Open http://SERVER-IP:8080/status. Your TV should be listed with status ok, and the pictures appear in Art Mode.
compose.yaml
services:
frame-tv-art-manager:
image: ghcr.io/mikeo7/frame-tv-art-manager:latest
container_name: frame-tv-art-manager
restart: unless-stopped
environment:
TV_IPS: "192.168.1.150" # your TV's address; comma-separate several
CLIENT_NAME: "Frame Art Manager"
ports:
- "8080:8080"
volumes:
- ./data:/data
docker compose up -d
docker compose logs -f frame-tv-art-manager

### Folders and permissions
Everything lives in the /data volume:
- /data/artwork is your collection. Mount a different host folder here if your art lives elsewhere, for example /volume1/photos/frame:/data/artwork.
- /data/tokens holds the TV's pairing token and the record of what was uploaded. Keep it across upgrades, or the TV will ask to pair again and existing uploads will be treated as yours.
If the container can't write to ./data, create the folders with mkdir -p data/artwork data/tokens. Set PUID
and PGID to control file ownership, or own the folders yourself, add user: "UID:GID", and leave PUID/PGID unset.

### Settings you'll likely want
Common settings (all optional except TV_IPS)
- Setting | Default | Purpose
- TV_IPS | required | TV address, or several separated by commas
- SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES | 30 | Time between syncs
- PORTRAIT_MODE | pad | Portraits on a gallery mat; or collage, crop
- ROTATION_INTERVAL_DAYS | 14 | How long each piece stays on a full TV
- MATTE_STYLE | none | Samsung matte for every upload
- UPLOAD_ENABLED, UPLOAD_TOKEN | off | Web and iPhone Shortcut uploads
- ARTWORK_SOURCES_FILE | unset | Download art from museums, Wikimedia Commons, NASA, and photo sites
- MCP_ENABLED, MCP_TOKEN | off | Let an AI assistant add and schedule art over MCP; the token needs at least 24 characters (AI art guide)
- LOCATION_TIMEZONE | UTC | Clock for power times, sun-following brightness, and seasonal collection dates
- MAX_LOCAL_FILE_SIZE_MB | 200 | Largest file accepted from the artwork folder (1–512); larger files are skipped with a warning
- DRY_RUN | false | Plan without changing anything
Every setting, with comments, is in .env.example.
On/off settings accept true/false, 1/0, yes/no, on/off, or y/n in any case.
Anything else, an unknown log level, or a bad TV address stops the service at startup with a clear error, so a typo can't silently turn a setting such as DRY_RUN off.

### Picture changes and TV controls
- Picture changes (on by default): every SLIDESHOW_INTERVAL minutes (default 15, any value from 1 to 1440) the manager puts another piece it uploaded on screen, in SLIDESHOW_TYPE order: shuffle (the default) shows every picture once, in a new random order each round, before any repeats; sequential goes in name order and wraps around. It changes the picture only while the TV is in Art Mode and can confirm what's on screen, never while someone is watching TV. It runs between syncs, so the interval isn't limited by SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES. SLIDESHOW_ENABLED=false turns it off and leaves the choice to the TV. SLIDESHOW_MODE=tv sets the TV's own slideshow instead, which on current firmware may need an Art Store subscription; SLIDESHOW_INTERVAL must then be 3, 15, 60, 720, or 1440.
- Brightness: a fixed BRIGHTNESS on the Frame's Art Mode scale of 0 to 10, or SOLAR_BRIGHTNESS_ENABLED=true with your latitude, longitude, and time zone to follow the sun between BRIGHTNESS_MIN and BRIGHTNESS_MAX (also 0 to 10). Values from 11 to 50, from the 0 to 50 scale earlier releases documented, are converted (30 becomes 6) with a warning; anything else outside 0 to 10 stops startup.
- Nightly power-off: AUTO_OFF_TIME=22:00 turns off TVs showing art and leaves TVs in use alone.
- Morning power-on: AUTO_ON_TIME (for example 07:00) together with TV_MAC wakes a single TV once a day, on the first sync in the AUTO_ON_GRACE_HOURS window (default 2), only if the TV is confirmed off or has dropped off the network; never when its state is unknown. TV_MAC on its own no longer wakes the TV. The magic packet goes to 255.255.255.255 and the TV's /24 broadcast address; set TV_WOL_BROADCAST to use one other broadcast address instead. Wake-on-LAN is a broadcast, which Docker's default bridge network doesn't pass to your LAN, so it needs network_mode: host.
Leave the brightness and power settings unset and the manager doesn't touch them.

### Monitoring and upgrades
- GET /live: the process is running (used by the container healthcheck).
- GET /ready and /health: 200 once the last sync succeeded, otherwise 503.
- GET /status: per-TV status, last error, rotation details, and credits for downloaded artwork as JSON. source_warning appears when an artwork source failed; the TVs still sync the art already on disk.
When UPLOAD_TOKEN is set, /status shows the last error and TV addresses only to requests signed in as frame with that token. Without credentials it returns the same fields with TVs numbered tv-1, tv-2, …, no error text, and "redacted": true.
Logs are structured JSON. To upgrade, run docker compose pull and docker compose up -d; your data folder carries over. Upgrading from a release before picture changes: the picture now changes every 15 minutes unless you set SLIDESHOW_ENABLED=false or SLIDESHOW_MODE=tv.
Never expose port 8080 to the internet; keep it on your home network or behind a TLS reverse proxy.

### Running without Docker
Build a single binary with the Go version in go.mod:
go build -o frame-tv-art-manager ./cmd/frame-tv-art-manager
TV_IPS=192.168.1.150 ARTWORK_DIR="$PWD/data/artwork" TOKEN_DIR="$PWD/data/tokens" ./frame-tv-art-manager

## Samsung Frame TV art from a Synology, Unraid, or TrueNAS NAS

URL: https://mikeo7.github.io/frame-tv-art-manager/guides/frame-tv-art-synology-unraid-truenas.html

Short answer: Frame TV Art Manager is a small Docker container, so any NAS that runs containers can keep your Frame in sync. On Synology use Container Manager's Projects, on Unraid add a container from the Docker tab, and on TrueNAS install a custom app from YAML. In each case you set TV_IPS, map a folder to /data, and approve the connection once on the TV.

### The same three things on every NAS
- A fixed IP for the TV, using a DHCP reservation in your router.
- A persistent folder mapped to /data. It holds artwork (your collection) and tokens (the pairing token and upload records). You can map your art share straight to /data/artwork instead.
- The right owner for files, set with PUID and PGID so you can still edit the artwork share over SMB.
Originals are kept. Each picture in the artwork folder is replaced by its prepared 3840×2160 version, and the untouched original is saved in the share's hidden .frame-tv-art-manager/originals folder. Allow about as much extra space as the pictures you add.

### Synology DSM (Container Manager)
- Install Container Manager from Package Center (DSM 7.2 or later).
- In File Station, create docker/frame-tv-art-manager with data/artwork and data/tokens inside it.
- Open Container Manager, go to Project, choose Create, pick that folder as the path, and choose to create a docker-compose.yml.
- Paste the compose file below, set your TV's address, and add PUID/PGID for the DSM user who owns the share. Running id yourname over SSH shows them; DSM users usually belong to group 100 (users).
- Finish the wizard to build and start the project, then approve the prompt on the TV.
- Copy pictures into docker/frame-tv-art-manager/data/artwork from File Station or over SMB.

### Unraid (Docker tab)
- Open the Docker tab and choose Add Container.
- Set Repository to ghcr.io/mikeo7/frame-tv-art-manager:latest and a name such as frame-tv-art-manager.
- Add a Path: container path /data, host path /mnt/user/appdata/frame-tv-art-manager. To use an existing share for art, add another path from /mnt/user/your-art-share to /data/artwork.
- Add a Variable TV_IPS with your TV's address, plus PUID=99 and PGID=100, Unraid's usual nobody:users owner for shares.
- Add a Port mapping 8080 to 8080 if you want the status page or uploader.
- Apply, then approve the prompt on the TV.
If you prefer compose files, the Compose Manager plugin accepts the same file as the Docker guide.

### TrueNAS SCALE / Community Edition
- Create a dataset, for example apps/frame-tv-art-manager, with data/artwork and data/tokens folders.
- Go to Apps, then Discover Apps, and choose Install via YAML from the menu (TrueNAS 24.10 and later use Docker for apps).
- Paste the compose file below with the host path changed to your dataset, such as /mnt/tank/apps/frame-tv-art-manager/data:/data.
- Set PUID/PGID to the user that owns the dataset; TrueNAS's built-in apps user is 568.
- Save, then approve the prompt on the TV.

### Compose file for any NAS
services:
frame-tv-art-manager:
image: ghcr.io/mikeo7/frame-tv-art-manager:latest
container_name: frame-tv-art-manager
restart: unless-stopped
environment:
TV_IPS: "192.168.1.150" # your TV's address; comma-separate several
CLIENT_NAME: "Frame Art Manager"
ports:
- "8080:8080"
volumes:
- ./data:/data
Add PUID and PGID under environment for your NAS. QNAP Container Station, OpenMediaVault, Portainer, and
anything else that accepts a compose file work the same way.

### Raspberry Pi, mini PC, or Mac
The image is built for amd64, arm64, and armv7, so a Raspberry Pi-class board, an Intel or AMD mini PC, or a Mac
running Docker all work. Preparing a 24-megapixel photo uses roughly 250 MB of memory, and each picture stays within a
512 MB budget by default (IMAGE_MAX_WORKING_MEMORY_MB).

### Network checklist
- The NAS and the TV must reach each other: same network, or routing between VLANs.
- Nothing needs to be opened to the internet. Keep port 8080 on your home network.
- The morning wake (AUTO_ON_TIME with TV_MAC) uses Wake-on-LAN, a broadcast that Docker's default bridge network doesn't forward, so it needs host networking. By default the packet goes to 255.255.255.255 and the TV's /24 broadcast address; TV_WOL_BROADCAST sends it to one other IPv4 broadcast address instead.
- If you turn on the MCP endpoint for an AI assistant, it uses the same port 8080 and stays on your home network too.

## Home Assistant and Samsung Frame TV art

URL: https://mikeo7.github.io/frame-tv-art-manager/guides/home-assistant-samsung-frame-tv-art.html

Short answer: Home Assistant is good at controlling the TV; Frame TV Art Manager is good at keeping its art collection in sync. Run the art manager as its own Docker container on your network, watch it from Home Assistant with a REST sensor on /status, and send pictures to it from automations with the upload endpoint. Everything stays local; no SmartThings cloud is involved.

### Why keep Frame art local
Home Assistant can reach a Samsung TV in two ways: locally over the network, or through Samsung's SmartThings
cloud. In June 2026 Samsung announced paid SmartThings API access, with a US$4.99-a-month personal
plan and free access ending after the third quarter of 2026. Frame TV Art Manager talks to the TV directly over your network,
so its art sync doesn't depend on SmartThings at all.

### Who does what
Splitting the work between Home Assistant and Frame TV Art Manager
- Job | Good fit
- Power, inputs, presence-based scenes | Home Assistant
- Keeping a folder of art on one or more Frames | Frame TV Art Manager
- Preparing pictures for 4K, portraits on a gallery mat | Frame TV Art Manager
- Rotating art when the TV is full | Frame TV Art Manager
- Changing the picture on screen, brightness, nightly power-off | Either, but only one of them

### Install it next to Home Assistant
If Home Assistant runs in Docker, add Frame TV Art Manager to the same host with the compose file from the
Docker guide. If you use Home Assistant OS, run Frame TV Art Manager on another
always-on machine, such as your NAS. The two only need to reach each other and the TV over the network.

### Watch sync health with a REST sensor
The /status endpoint returns JSON with last_sync_ok, last_error, and a tvs object with each TV's
status, image count, and rotation details. Add this to configuration.yaml:
rest:
- resource: http://SERVER-IP:8080/status
scan_interval: 300
authentication: basic
username: frame
password: !secret frame_upload_token
sensor:
- name: Frame art last sync OK
value_template: "{{ value_json.last_sync_ok }}"
- name: Frame art last error
value_template: "{{ value_json.last_error | default('', true) | truncate(250) }}"
The three sign-in lines matter once UPLOAD_TOKEN is set: /status then shows the last error and TV addresses only to requests signed in as
frame with that token, and anonymous requests get the same fields with TVs numbered tv-1, tv-2, …, no error text, and "redacted": true.
Put the token in secrets.yaml as frame_upload_token. Without UPLOAD_TOKEN, /status is open and the sign-in lines are harmless.
Then alert yourself when last_sync_ok stays false. A source_warning field appears when an online art source failed; the TVs still sync the art already on disk.
/ready returns HTTP 200 or 503 if you'd rather use a simple binary check; it needs no password.

### Send pictures from an automation
Turn on the uploader (UPLOAD_ENABLED=true and a 16-character-plus UPLOAD_TOKEN). Home Assistant's
shell_command can then post a JPEG or PNG, for example a snapshot saved by another automation:
# configuration.yaml
shell_command:
send_to_frame: "/config/scripts/send_to_frame.sh {{ filename }}"
#!/bin/sh
# /config/scripts/send_to_frame.sh (chmod +x); the token lives in a file only root can read
TOKEN="$(cat /config/.frame_upload_token)"
curl --fail -u "frame:$TOKEN" -F "file=@/config/www/frame/$1" http://SERVER-IP:8080/upload
Keep the token out of configuration.yaml, and only pass simple file names you control. Uploads are handled one at a time; a second
upload sent at the same moment gets HTTP 429 and should be retried.

### Avoid two tools fighting over the TV
- Frame TV Art Manager changes the picture on screen every 15 minutes by default. If a Home Assistant automation picks the art, set SLIDESHOW_ENABLED=false, or the two will keep replacing each other's choice.
- Brightness and power settings are left alone unless you set them. If Home Assistant already manages them, leave the matching settings unset.
- It never deletes art it didn't upload, so pictures you push another way stay on the TV.
- Each tool that connects to the TV may need its own one-time Allow on the TV. Use a clear CLIENT_NAME so you know which prompt is which.

Q: Can Home Assistant control Samsung Frame TV Art Mode?
A: Home Assistant's Samsung integrations can control power and, with some community integrations, parts of Art Mode. For keeping a collection of art on the TV, Frame TV Art Manager runs alongside Home Assistant and handles uploads, preparation, and rotation.

Q: Does Frame TV Art Manager need SmartThings?
A: No. It connects to the TV directly on your local network, so Samsung's SmartThings API changes don't affect it.

Q: Is there a Home Assistant add-on for Frame TV Art Manager?
A: No. It runs as a standalone Docker container. Home Assistant OS users can run it on another machine such as a NAS.

Q: How do I know if the Frame art sync failed?
A: Poll http://SERVER-IP:8080/status with a REST sensor and watch last_sync_ok, or check /ready, which returns 503 when the last sync failed.

## How to send photos from an iPhone or Apple Photos to a Samsung Frame TV

URL: https://mikeo7.github.io/frame-tv-art-manager/guides/apple-photos-to-samsung-frame-tv.html

Short answer: turn on Frame TV Art Manager's upload page and send photos to it from your iPhone, iPad, or Mac. The quickest way is the upload page in Safari; an iPhone Shortcut or a Mac script can send favorites or an album on a schedule. Photos join the artwork folder and reach every Frame TV on the next sync, within 30 minutes by default.

### Turn on the uploader
The uploader is off by default. Add two settings to your compose file and restart the container:
environment:
TV_IPS: "192.168.1.150"
UPLOAD_ENABLED: "true"
UPLOAD_TOKEN: "a-long-random-password-of-16-plus-characters"
ports:
- "8080:8080"
Sign in with username frame and your UPLOAD_TOKEN as the password. Each upload can be up to 20 MB (MAX_DOWNLOAD_SIZE_MB).

### Quickest: the upload page in Safari
Open http://SERVER-IP:8080/upload in Safari, sign in, tap the drop area, and choose photos. The page sends
them one by one and shows each result. On a Mac you can drag files onto it. It accepts JPEG and PNG; if a HEIC photo is
rejected, use the Shortcut below, which converts explicitly.

### Build an iPhone or iPad Shortcut
First make the sign-in value the Shortcut needs. On a Mac or Linux computer, run this with your own token and copy the output:
printf '%s' 'frame:YOUR_UPLOAD_TOKEN' | base64
- Create the shortcut. In Shortcuts, tap +, and name it "Send to Frame TV".
- Find the photos. Add Find Photos, filter for Favorites or an album, add Media Type is Image, and set a small Limit while testing.
- Loop over them. Add Repeat with Each.
- Convert to JPEG. Inside the loop, add Convert Image to JPEG. iPhone photos are usually HEIC, which the uploader doesn't accept.
- Upload each photo. Add Get Contents of URL: URL http://SERVER-IP:8080/upload, method POST, request body Form with a File field named file, and a header Authorization set to Basic, a space, and your encoded value.
- Test it. Each photo should return "File imported successfully", or "File already exists (deduplicated)" if it was sent before.
To run it on a schedule, use the Automation tab: Time of Day, run immediately, and pick the shortcut. Identical files are
skipped, but if iOS produces a slightly different JPEG of the same photo on a later run, it's stored as a new picture, so keep the album focused.

### Send favorites from a Mac automatically
The free third-party tool osxphotos exports favorites or an album as JPEGs, and a short script uploads them.
Give your terminal Full Disk Access in System Settings, install osxphotos (for example pipx install osxphotos), and save this as ~/frame-tv-sync.sh:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
SERVER="http://192.168.1.20:8080" # the Frame TV Art Manager server, not the TV
UPLOAD_TOKEN="your-upload-token"
EXPORT_DIR="$HOME/Pictures/frame-tv-export"
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH"
mkdir -p "$EXPORT_DIR"
osxphotos export "$EXPORT_DIR" --favorite \
--convert-to-jpeg --jpeg-quality 0.95 \
--skip-live --skip-raw --update --cleanup
for file in "$EXPORT_DIR"/*.jpeg "$EXPORT_DIR"/*.jpg; do
[ -f "$file" ] || continue
curl --fail --silent --show-error -u "frame:$UPLOAD_TOKEN" \
-F "file=@$file" "$SERVER/upload"
echo
done
Replace --favorite with --album "Frame TV" to send an album. Run it hourly with a LaunchAgent whose
